description: Only paths listed in forkFirst (auto --ours) or upstreamFirst (auto --theirs) are resolved without an agent. Everything else — whether or not it appears in manualReview — is agent-reviewed. manualReview is a non-exhaustive hint list of known hard shared hotspots, not a closed set. unionPaths are agent-reviewed: keep fork-only symbols and take upstream additions; never drop upstream exports that in-tree consumers import. package.json is union-merged (upstream base + fork-only scripts/deps). bun.lock is regenerated after manifests. Agents SHOULD extend this file when they learn a recurring rule (add a forkFirst/upstreamFirst/manualReview/unionPaths prefix or packageJson.dropScripts entry) so the next sync is cheaper. apps/sim/lib/copilot/generated/ is NO LONGER upstreamFirst (moved to manualReview on run 2026-08-06-4). The fork carries a hand-edit there (Superagent task description, Google Docs GFM guidance) that exists in NO generator source, and `bun run mship:generate` cannot regenerate it in this checkout because scripts/sync-tool-catalog.ts reads a sibling repo (../copilot/) the fork does not have. Two consecutive runs (2026-08-06-3, 2026-08-06-4) confirmed the natural three-way merge preserves that sentence while auto --theirs would have deleted it. Let the merge run and use a VERIFY-ONLY mustEdit that asserts the sentence is still present. IMPORTANT (run 2026-08-06-5): that verify-only assertion is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. Upstream #5410/#5656 deleted seven catalog entries the fork still routes (Superagent, Research, UserMemory, MoveFile, MoveFileFolder, RenameFile, RenameFileFolder) and inserted ShareFile/Search at the same offsets, so the natural merge kept the fork's GFM sentence but grafted it onto share_file's `action` param while deleting the Superagent entry that owned it. Assert BOTH the sentence AND the presence of every fork-consumed export. Second silent-breakage class from the same run: packages/db/migrations/meta/_journal.json AUTO-MERGES (no conflict markers, so no child ever looks at it) into a journal with duplicate idx values whenever both sides add migrations at the same index. Always diff the journal after the merge even when git reports it clean.

packageJson.sharedDependencyVersionsNote: On a version-only conflict for a dependency BOTH sides declare, take upstream's version. Fork-only deps (sanitize-html, selenium-webdriver, soap, ...) are kept by the union. Established run 2026-08-06-5: upstream #5848 bumped sharp 0.34.3 -> 0.35.3 and js-yaml 4.2.0 -> 4.3.0 for security advisories; pinning the fork's older version would silently keep the advisory. Regenerate bun.lock after manifests; never hand-merge bun.lock.
packageJson.overridesNote: IMPORTANT (run 2026-08-07): the version rule must be applied to `overrides` blocks too, and to BOTH manifests. The root package.json `overrides` auto-merges to upstream's version, but apps/sim/package.json carries a FORK-ONLY `overrides` block that git never reconciles against it. This run the root resolved to next 16.2.12 (upstream #5890 + #6077, both security-advisory bumps) while apps/sim/package.json still pinned `next`/`@next/env` to 16.2.6 inside the conflict region - a split pin that reintroduces the advisory and can desync @next/swc. After every merge, diff `next` across root overrides, root optionalDependencies (@next/swc-*), apps/sim dependencies, and apps/sim overrides; they must all be the same version.

dedupeOnUnionNote: Union hazard class discovered on run 2026-08-06-5. On these files upstream re-adds, at a NEW position, a symbol the fork already defines elsewhere in the SAME file (fork inherited it earlier or authored a superset). A naive union produces duplicate object-literal keys / duplicate exports / duplicate else-if branches, which is a hard TypeScript error, not a lint nit. Measured cases: env.ts (XAI_API_KEY_1..3 already at fork L168-171, upstream re-adds them next to KIMI_API_KEY_1..3), api-keys.ts (fork already has `provider !== 'xai'` and `else if (provider === 'xai')`), uploads/config.ts (fork already exports BLOB_CONFIG), providers/utils.ts (fork retains SambaNova + OpenRouter in the hosted gate). Rule: union the genuinely NEW symbols only, then grep the merged file for duplicate identifiers.

manualReviewNotes.apps/sim/lib/workspaces/policy.ts: Both sides independently rewrote the SAME `!isBillingEnabled` branch of `evaluateWorkspaceCreationPolicy` — the branch Arena actually runs. The fork forces every workspace to workspaceMode ORGANIZATION and tracks personal-ness on the fork-authored `workspace.is_personal` column (migration 0248_workspace_is_personal.sql, commit `ccfdd45292` "Personal workspace attaching to Org"), gating non-admins to one workspace. Upstream #5918 keeps the mode split and lets plain members create org workspaces freely once billing is off, adding `observedOrganizationId`, `blockedReasonCode` and a billing-identity lock. Never auto-resolve this file — it is a product decision (asked as Q1 on run 2026-08-07 / PR #690).
manualReviewNotes.apps/sim/lib/invitations/: The fork has never touched this directory, so upstream #5918's join-time workspace sweep lands WHOLE via auto-merge with zero conflict markers. Accepting an organization invitation now reassigns the joiner's owned workspaces (organizationId + billedAccountUserId) into that organization. A clean merge here is a live behaviour change — audit it every sync even when git reports no conflict.
manualReviewNotes.apps/sim/tools/exa/: Upstream #6074 refreshed the whole integration against the live API and retired `exa_research` (/research/v1 returns HTTP 410 RESEARCH_RETIRED — the fork's operation is hard-broken in production). Upstream's block routes saved `exa_research` workflows to the new `exa_agent` and preserves the research output shape, and it already carries the fork's four crawl/published-date subBlocks. Upstream-first is correct here; the only fork re-apply is the `apiKey` subBlock (`required: false, hidden: true` — Arena always supplies the hosted key). Same shape for firecrawl: upstream extracted `firecrawlHosting()` from the inline `hosting` blocks the fork wrote.
manualReviewNotes.apps/sim/lib/copilot/tools/server/files/: Upstream retired the copilot `delete_file` / `delete_file_folder` tools with no replacement: `delete-file.ts` is DELETED silently (fork never modified it since base, so git takes the deletion with no conflict), the catalog + schema entries vanish, and `tool-schemas-v1.ts` auto-merges to zero `delete_file` occurrences. The fork-only `apps/sim/local-copilot/` still advertises and delegates both tool names, so accepting the deletion breaks Arena's local copilot at runtime, not at build time. Restore additively (run 2026-08-06-5 precedent) and assert the exports after every merge.
